segments.copy: If your stomach looks like this on a GLP-1, watch this. Especially if you're eating less, but feeling more bloated.
segments.visual: H01: Illustrative adult woman, clothed side profile in bedroom mirror, palm lightly resting on waistband; neutral expression, no exaggerated swelling.
segments.purpose: Immediate recognition; the word this has a visible referent.

segments.copy: You sit down to a small meal. A few bites later, your stomach feels stretched and tight. And you wonder how so little food can leave you feeling so full.
segments.visual: H02: Overhead lunch plate; woman puts fork down beside a modest meal.
segments.purpose: Name the contradiction that earns the explanation.

segments.copy: By the afternoon, you're loosening your waistband. The outfit you felt good in this morning is suddenly the one you want to change out of.
segments.visual: H03: Seated three-quarter office view; discreet waistband adjustment beneath desk.
segments.purpose: Move from symptom to daily consequence.
segments.evidence: Original scenario informed by local bloating research

segments.copy: You wanted to feel more comfortable in your body. Now you're checking your stomach before you leave the house and wondering how you'll feel after dinner.
segments.visual: H04: Hallway wide shot; woman pauses with handbag and keys, glances toward mirror.
segments.purpose: Establish the desired outcome: comfort and participation.
segments.evidence: Original scenario; not a measured audience prevalence claim

segments.copy: Maybe you've tried peppermint tea, cut out a favorite food, or picked up another digestive supplement. And you're still trying to work out what actually sets the bloating off.
segments.visual: H05: Kitchen overhead; hand moves handwritten food diary beside plain tea mug. No remedy stack or discarded medication.
segments.purpose: Acknowledge effort without declaring treatments ineffective.

segments.copy: That is the frustrating part. You keep looking for something you ate, when a change in how your digestion works could also be part of the picture.
segments.visual: P01: Presenter medium shot, direct eye contact; quiet pause after first sentence.
segments.purpose: Shift from food blame to a broader explanation.
segments.evidence: Qualified explanation; does not diagnose the viewer

segments.copy: GLP-1 medicines such as Wegovy can slow how quickly your stomach empties. Bloating is also a listed side effect. So this deserves more attention than simply blaming your last meal.
segments.visual: S01: Authentic prescribing-information excerpt with restrained highlights on stomach emptying and bloating.
segments.purpose: Introduce external factual authority without inventing a clinician.

segments.copy: Your stomach does more than hold food. Its muscles mix what you eat and gradually move it into your small intestine. That process takes time.
segments.visual: S02: Isolated stomach-to-duodenum educational model showing mixing and measured passage; no medicine or product in frame.
segments.purpose: Explain the process in ordinary language.
segments.evidence: General anatomy; schematic illustration, not diagnostic imagery

segments.copy: When your stomach empties more slowly, that lingering fullness can make more sense. The amount on your plate is only one part of the story.
segments.visual: S03: Simple clock-and-meal schematic showing elapsed time and lingering fullness label; no accumulating sludge or complete blockage.
segments.purpose: Return the explanation to the opening small-meal experience.
segments.evidence: Qualified context; no universal causal attribution

segments.copy: Gas and constipation can contribute to bloating too. That is why the same swollen feeling does not always have the same explanation, even for people taking the same medication.
segments.visual: S04: Distinct colon schematic with modest gas pockets and separate constipation label; no stomach cutaway reuse.
segments.purpose: Avoid forcing every symptom into one cause.

segments.copy: And adding more to your routine isn't automatically the answer. Some people get more gas with extra fiber. The type, the amount, and your own response all matter.
segments.visual: S05: Two neutral fiber ingredient cards beside measuring-spoon silhouette; no product efficacy comparison.
segments.purpose: Explain why selection and individual tolerance matter.

segments.copy: So the useful question becomes: what belongs in a daily digestive routine for you? Something with clear ingredients, a manageable daily serving, and a routine you can actually keep up with.
segments.visual: P02: Presenter holds blank three-item card; editor adds Ingredients / Directions / Personal fit.
segments.purpose: Establish honest selection criteria before the brand.

segments.copy: One combination you'll see is celery juice powder, prebiotic fiber, and chlorophyll. Three different ingredients, which are worth understanding before you decide whether to add them to your day.
segments.visual: I01: Three tabletop ingredient stations, celery powder, fiber sample and green pigment reference, separately labeled.
segments.purpose: Introduce the actual listed ingredients without unproven treatment claims.
segments.evidence: Current Motilli product page; ingredient identity is seller-reported

segments.copy: Prebiotic fiber provides food for bacteria in your gut. That's its role. Your own tolerance still matters, especially when bloating is the reason you're looking at digestive support.
segments.visual: I02: Microscopic-style schematic of bacteria using fiber substrate; no good-versus-evil characters or instant gas disappearance.
segments.purpose: Give the technical term a job and retain the relevant limitation.
segments.evidence: General prebiotic role; not evidence of Motilli bloating efficacy

segments.copy: Celery juice powder is the plant ingredient. Chlorophyll is the green pigment found in plants; supplements may use a related form called chlorophyllin. Those names tell you what's included.
segments.visual: I03: Celery stalk macro transitions at Chlorophyll to distinct leaf-pigment macro with chlorophyllin label.
segments.purpose: Clarify names without inventing a prokinetic or gas-neutralizing action.
segments.evidence: Current ingredient list names sodium copper chlorophyllin

segments.copy: Motilli brings those ingredients together in a daily digestive-support gummy. The practical difference is having them in one simple routine, with the ingredients and directions available to review before you buy.
segments.visual: PR01: First verified Motilli bottle reveal on bedside surface; real label readable, camera settles.
segments.purpose: Match product to the criteria already introduced.
segments.evidence: Current seller-listed formula and format; no proof of disease-specific efficacy

segments.copy: And if you're tired of swallowing another capsule or mixing another drink, the gummy format may be the part you appreciate first. You simply chew it.
segments.visual: PR02: Hands open verified bottle and place gummies on clean palm; no swallowing simulation.
segments.purpose: Answer format objection through convenience rather than absorption superiority.

segments.copy: Motilli's directions are two gummies before bed with a full glass of water. That gives you a straightforward routine to discuss with your prescriber alongside anything else you're taking.
segments.visual: PR03: Bedside overhead, exactly two current-reference gummies and full water glass; hand sets bottle beside them.
segments.purpose: Make use understandable without asserting universal medication compatibility.
segments.evidence: Current product directions; advise individual discussion

segments.copy: If you decide to try it, pay attention to how you actually feel. Keep track of your bloating and comfort, so you can evaluate your own experience.
segments.visual: H06: Close-up simple symptom journal being filled in; no fabricated improving scores or guaranteed timeline.
segments.purpose: Replace borrowed week-by-week testimonial with a realistic evaluation.

segments.copy: Because the goal is easy to picture: getting dressed without planning around your waistband, enjoying a meal without spending the evening focused on your stomach, and feeling present when you're out.
segments.visual: F01: Original imagined-life scene: wide dining table, woman engaged in conversation. Small Imagine everyday comfort label; no before/after transformation.
segments.purpose: Resolve opening concerns as an aspiration, not a treatment result.

segments.copy: If you'd like to take a closer look, the link below takes you to Motilli. You can review the formula, the daily routine, and the available bottle options there.
segments.visual: PR04: Verified live product-page screen capture showing formula and bottle options; no price unless freshly checked.
segments.purpose: Make click destination specific and useful.

segments.copy: Motilli also offers a ninety-day money-back guarantee, starting when your order arrives. It covers opened bottles too, so opening the bottle doesn't end your chance to request a refund.
segments.visual: PR05: Real bottle with editor-rendered guarantee card: 90 days from delivery / Opened bottles included / Terms apply.
segments.purpose: State the actual risk reversal; no guaranteed result or no-return claim.

segments.copy: If you're ready to explore a simpler digestive routine, tap below to see Motilli. Start with the details, and decide whether it belongs in your routine.
segments.visual: PR06: Clean verified bottle and two gummies, See Motilli button graphic; stable final frame.
segments.purpose: One clear next action with no invented scarcity.
segments.evidence: Brand action; no medical outcome guarantee
